back: The whole way of life of a people: language, beliefs, values, customs, food, dress, music, dance, crafts and ceremonies.
Many different cultures, languages and ways of life existing side by side in one society.
A language that developed among, and has long been spoken by, a people of a particular area.
Chewa, Chibarwe, English, Kalanga, Koisan, Nambya, Ndau, Ndebele, Shangani, Shona, sign language, Sotho, Tonga, Tswana, Venda, Xhosa.
Venda: Beitbridge. Nambya: Hwange. Tonga: Zambezi valley (Binga).

front: Why were many Tonga families moved in the late 1950s?
back: Lake Kariba, created by the Kariba Dam, flooded their land along the Zambezi.

front: Give four reasons for upholding indigenous languages and cultures.
back: Identity, heritage, unity in diversity, equality and rights, better learning, tourism and creative income.

front: Name four ways of upholding smaller languages.
back: Speak them at home; teach them in schools with books; community radio and TV; culture days and festivals; record elders.

front: Is language the same as culture?
back: No: language is one part of culture, which also includes beliefs, food, dress, music, dance, crafts and ceremonies.
